tasks.short: Write and check the design docs for new Power BI reports and AFAS extracts before anything gets built.

today.trigger: An HR or finance stakeholder asks for a new dashboard or a change, for example a 90-day retention view per site or a verzuim report for the OR.
steps: Meet the requester and note the questions, filters and audience
Look up the AFAS Profit fields, Recruitee exports and existing Power BI datasets that hold the data
Write a spec in Word or SharePoint: sources, joins, measure definitions (DAX), refresh, access roles
Check the spec against AVG/GDPR rules: minimum group sizes, who may see sickness data
Review it with the requester and the HR Director, then build or hand it to a contractor
drudgery: Copying field names and table structures from AFAS connectors by hand
Re-documenting measures that already exist in other reports
Keeping old specs in sync after changes
today.time_sinks: Hunting down which AFAS GetConnector or Power BI measure already holds a definition, and rewriting the same privacy and access sections for every spec.

lenses.faster: An LLM drafts the spec from the meeting notes plus the existing Power BI model metadata, so the analyst edits a filled template instead of starting blank. Looking up fields and existing measures disappears.
lenses.autonomous: Every time a Power BI dataset is published, a script extracts tables, measures and row-level security roles and regenerates the reference documentation on SharePoint.
lenses.ambitious: Every report and measure at Noordhaven gets a current, searchable definition (what counts as a hire, as verzuim, as day 90), so HR and finance stop arguing about numbers.
lenses.joy: No more copying column names or rewriting the GDPR paragraph; the analyst spends the time on what the question really is.
lenses.options: For each request the model drafts two or three designs (one page vs drill-through, site vs team level) with the trade-offs on privacy and refresh cost.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the spec template, the metric glossary and the review checklist, and checks AI-drafted specs rather than writing them.
reach: Draft data definitions for FP&A Analysts' headcount and labour cost reports
Write privacy and access sections the HR Director now writes for the OR

tasks.human_edge: Pinning down what the requester actually needs, and judging privacy and OR sensitivities (for example, whether a site-level verzuim view singles out a small team).
tasks.pattern_why: Unstructured input (meeting notes, requests) becomes a structured spec inside a fixed template; model metadata extraction itself is deterministic, and the output is easy to check.

in_practice.trigger: New request logged in the HR analytics Teams channel or Planner, or a Power BI dataset publish.
steps: Script pulls dataset metadata (tables, measures, RLS roles) and AFAS connector field lists
LLM drafts the spec from the request notes, metadata and the metric glossary
Automated check flags measures without a glossary definition and groups below the minimum size
Analyst edits, decides open questions and sends to the requester for sign-off
Approved spec is filed on SharePoint and linked from the report
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves every spec; the HR Director signs off any report showing sickness or individual-level data.
systems: Power BI (XMLA endpoint or Tabular Editor)
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint spec library with version history

evidence.claim: Power BI Copilot can describe datasets and draft report pages and DAX from natural language.
Model metadata (tables, measures, roles) can be extracted by script from a Power BI dataset.
evidence.source: Tabular Editor / Power BI XMLA endpoint

evidence.claim: LLMs draft usable technical specs from notes and metadata when given a template.

risks: Drafts look complete but carry wrong joins or measure logic that nobody checks
Personal data in metadata or notes sent to a model outside the EU tenant
Specs auto-generated but not read, so the review step becomes a stamp
research_questions: How many report requests per month come in, and how long does a spec take today?
Does Noordhaven's Power BI licence allow XMLA read access to extract metadata?
Is there an agreed metric glossary, or does that have to be built first?
Can an LLM within the Microsoft 365 tenant be used under the current DPIA?

tasks.short: Track HR tech and labour market trends to decide which tools and HR services to add or improve.

today.trigger: Budget round, a vendor pitch, a contract renewal (Recruitee, Studytube), or a question from the HR Director about what other logistics firms do.
steps: Read vendor newsletters, LinkedIn posts and trade press on HR tech and logistics labour markets
Pull labour market figures for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo from UWV and CBS
Compare with own data: time to hire, flex share, 90-day retention per site
Write a short memo or slide deck with options for the HR Director
drudgery: Reading through marketing material to find the few relevant facts
Downloading and reshaping CBS and UWV tables each time
Rebuilding the same comparison deck every half year
today.time_sinks: Scanning sources by hand and reformatting public statistics so they can sit next to AFAS and Recruitee figures.

lenses.faster: An AI research assistant summarises sources with citations and a scheduled script pulls CBS and UWV data into Power BI, so the analyst starts from a sourced brief.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly job refreshes regional vacancy and wage data next to Noordhaven's own hiring metrics and flags shifts, for example rising forklift driver tightness in Venlo.
lenses.ambitious: A standing regional labour market view per site and role family, used in workforce planning, CAO talks and choices between flex agencies and own hires.
lenses.joy: Less wading through vendor marketing; more time on the question of what actually helps fill roles that last past 90 days.
lenses.options: For each decision (new assessment tool, agency mix, onboarding app) the model lays out three or four options with costs, evidence quality and fit to the CAO and OR consent rules.
lenses.altitude: The analyst designs the trend watch: sources, refresh, thresholds and the question list, and checks AI summaries instead of reading everything.
reach: Market data for recruiters' sourcing and pay-range choices
Input for the Compensation and Benefits Specialist's wage benchmarks
Workforce scenarios for FP&A Analysts' budget

tasks.human_edge: Judging which trends matter for a 1,200-person logistics firm with a works council, and weighing vendor claims against what Noordhaven can actually adopt.
tasks.pattern_why: The analyst leads the judgment and the advice; AI gathers, summarises and lays out options, while public data refresh is plain scheduled software.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly schedule plus ad hoc questions from the HR Director or a contract renewal date in the contract register.
steps: Scheduled pull of CBS StatLine and UWV regional data into the Power BI model
AI research assistant drafts a sourced brief on the question asked
Analyst checks sources, removes vendor hype and adds Noordhaven's own figures
Analyst writes the recommendation and shares it with the HR Director
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst verifies every cited claim and owns the recommendation; tool choices that touch employee data go to the OR and DPO.
data_needed: Regional labour market data per site
Own hiring and retention metrics from AFAS and Recruitee
Question list from the HR Director

evidence.claim: CBS StatLine publishes open labour market tables with an API.
AI research tools produce cited web summaries on a topic.
The 'markets and products' framing applies here only as HR services and tool choices; time on it may be lower than O*NET suggests.

risks: AI summaries repeat vendor claims or invent sources
Trends tracked that never feed a decision, so the work is wasted
Buying AI hiring tools that count as high-risk under the EU AI Act without the needed checks
research_questions: Which decisions in the past year used trend analysis, and did it change the outcome?
Is regional UWV and CBS data detailed enough per site and role family (forklift, warehouse, planner)?
How much of the analyst's time actually goes to this task today?

role.altitude: From building reports and memos to running the HR data system: metric glossary, automated documentation, data pipelines and quality checks, with the analyst reviewing what AI drafts.
reach: Workforce and labour cost analysis for FP&A Analysts
Pay benchmarking support for the Compensation and Benefits Specialist
Sourcing market data for the Recruiters
Data checks on payroll output with the Payroll Specialist
DPIA and OR documentation for HR data use with the HR Director
role.ceiling_note: Limited by data quality in AFAS and Recruitee, AVG/GDPR and OR consent for new uses of employee data, and the need for a person to own every number shown to management; perhaps 40 to 50 percent of hours on these two tasks can be freed.
skills_to_grow: Metadata-driven documentation and Power BI model scripting
Prompt and template design for LLM steps with checkable output
Data protection and EU AI Act basics for HR analytics
Python for scheduled data pulls (CBS, UWV, agency portals)
Advising leadership with options and trade-offs
role.ambitious_version: One trusted HR data model across AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube and the agency portals, with documented definitions and a live view of the North Star per site, plus labour market context, so HR and finance plan hiring, flex use and onboarding from the same numbers.
